entry.title: Tamil Nadu’s Solar Journey: From Early Adopter to Leading State

link.title: Tamil Nadu’s Solar Journey: From Early Adopter to Leading State

entry.content:
Tamil Nadu has been one of India’s front-runners in solar power. High solar irradiation, early policy focus, and big utility-scale projects have made the state a model for solar inception and growth.

Sun and policy: a strong start

The state gets some of the best solar irradiation in the country, with long sunny hours ideal for both rooftop and ground-mounted plants. Tamil Nadu’s solar policy and the growth of the Kamuthi solar park — once among the world’s largest single-location solar plants — put the state on the global solar map.

Rooftop and open access

Alongside large projects, Tamil Nadu pushed rooftop solar and open access for commercial and industrial consumers. Net metering and group net metering helped homes and businesses adopt solar and reduce grid dependency. Today, the state remains among the top in India for installed solar capacity and continues to attract new projects and investment.

For anyone looking at solar in Tamil Nadu, the combination of strong sunshine and a mature market makes it an ideal place to go solar.
entry.summary: How Tamil Nadu became one of India's top states for solar power with strong sun and progressive policies.

entry.title: Solar Inception in India: How the National Solar Mission Started a Revolution

link.title: Solar Inception in India: How the National Solar Mission Started a Revolution

entry.content:
India’s large-scale solar story began with the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission (NSM), launched in 2010. The mission set an ambitious target of 20 GW of solar capacity by 2022 and put solar energy at the centre of the country’s clean-energy plans.

Why the National Solar Mission mattered

The NSM was the first nationwide framework to promote both grid-connected and off-grid solar. It encouraged utility-scale solar parks, rooftop solar, and off-grid applications in rural areas. Tariff-based competitive bidding and incentives for manufacturers helped bring down costs and scale deployment.

From 20 GW to 100 GW and beyond

Targets were later raised to 100 GW of solar by 2022, with 40 GW from rooftop and 60 GW from utility-scale. Although the 2022 deadline saw mixed progress, India’s total solar capacity has grown to one of the largest in the world. States like Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Karnataka, and Gujarat led the way with strong irradiation and supportive policies.

That early “solar inception” — the NSM and follow-on policies — set the base for today’s solar market in India and made solar a mainstream option for homes and industries.
entry.summary: How India's National Solar Mission and early policies kickstarted solar power adoption across the country.

entry.title: Record Low Solar Tariffs in Latest SECI Auctions

link.title: Record Low Solar Tariffs in Latest SECI Auctions

entry.content:
SECI’s latest round of solar project auctions has again pushed tariffs to record lows. Winning bids in several ISTS-connected and state-specific tenders have come in well below ₹2.50/kWh, reflecting intense competition and lower module and financing costs.

For commercial and industrial offtakers and state discoms, these tariffs mean long-term power purchase at very competitive rates. For developers, margins remain thin and execution efficiency is key. The trend underlines India’s position as one of the lowest-cost solar markets globally.
entry.summary: SECI's latest solar auctions see record-low tariffs. What it means for developers and offtakers in India.

entry.title: Solar + Storage: Incentives and Pilot Projects in India

link.title: Solar + Storage: Incentives and Pilot Projects in India

entry.content:
Central and state governments are stepping up support for solar combined with battery storage. New guidelines and pilot schemes aim to improve grid stability and enable round-the-clock renewable supply for C&I and discoms.

Tamil Nadu and other states have expressed interest in storage-linked solar tenders. For businesses weighing backup and peak-shaving, incentive-linked storage is becoming more relevant. We summarise the latest policy and pilot updates.
entry.summary: Latest incentives and pilot projects for solar plus battery storage in India and Tamil Nadu.

entry.title: ALMM List Update: Approved Solar Modules for India

link.title: ALMM List Update: Approved Solar Modules for India

entry.content:
The Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) for solar PV modules has been updated again. New domestic and overseas manufacturers have been added, and some models have been removed. Projects under government schemes and many state tenders must use ALMM-listed modules.

For EPC contractors and developers, staying on top of ALMM is essential to avoid delays and compliance issues. We track the latest list and eligibility for PM Surya Ghar and other subsidised programmes.
entry.summary: Latest ALMM list update and which solar modules are approved for use in government and subsidised projects in India.

entry.title: Tamil Nadu’s New Solar Policy Highlights

link.title: Tamil Nadu’s New Solar Policy Highlights

entry.content:
Tamil Nadu has released an updated solar policy with clearer targets for rooftop, open access, and utility-scale capacity. The policy emphasises faster approvals, group net metering for housing societies, and support for MSMEs and industries.

Rooftop subsidies are aligned with the central PM Surya Ghar scheme. For open access, the state has simplified banking and wheeling provisions. Here are the highlights that matter most for developers and consumers.
entry.summary: Key highlights of Tamil Nadu's updated solar policy for rooftop, open access, and utility-scale projects.

entry.title: Solar Panel Price Trends in India (Oct 2025–Feb 2026)

link.title: Solar Panel Price Trends in India (Oct 2025–Feb 2026)

entry.content:
Module and balance-of-system costs have continued to ease in India over the last few months. Factors include higher domestic manufacturing, ALMM expansion, and competitive imports in segments where they are permitted.

Rooftop system prices (₹/W) have moved down for both residential and C&I segments. We look at the main drivers and what to expect for the next quarter when planning a solar installation.
entry.summary: How solar panel and system prices have moved in India from October 2025 to February 2026.

entry.title: Green Open Access Rules: Boon for C&I Solar

link.title: Green Open Access Rules: Boon for C&I Solar

entry.content:
Green Open Access rules have been simplified at the central level and adopted by many states. Minimum contract demand for green OA has been reduced, making it viable for more commercial and industrial consumers to source solar and other renewable power through open access.

Banking, surcharges, and cross-subsidy components continue to be refined. For industries in Tamil Nadu and elsewhere, green OA is now a practical route to cheaper, cleaner power. We summarise the key changes and how to evaluate OA vs rooftop.
entry.summary: How Green Open Access rules are making it easier for commercial and industrial consumers to source solar power in India.

entry.title: Karnataka vs Tamil Nadu: Which State Is Better for Solar?

link.title: Karnataka vs Tamil Nadu: Which State Is Better for Solar?

entry.content:
Both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu rank among the top states for installed solar capacity. Karnataka has strong irradiation and an early mover advantage; Tamil Nadu has caught up with large utility projects and a growing rooftop and open-access market.

We compare net metering, open access, subsidies, and approval timelines so C&I and residential consumers can weigh the two. The “better” state depends on your load profile, location, and whether you prefer rooftop or offsite solar.
entry.summary: Compare solar policies, irradiation, and project economics in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu for C&I and rooftop.

entry.title: Floating Solar in India: Government Push and Projects

link.title: Floating Solar in India: Government Push and Projects

entry.content:
Floating solar is gaining momentum in India as states and central agencies look to use water bodies for generation without consuming land. Several tenders have been floated for reservoirs, dams, and canals.

Pilot projects and larger installations are under way in states including Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Maharashtra. We look at the policy push, typical project sizes, and what developers and EPC players need to know about floating PV.
entry.summary: Central and state support for floating solar in India and key projects coming up.
